what: a modelled M14 thread on a 14.6 mm boss, slightly thicker than the thread (refused: the face is too far from the thread's diameter)
method: ISO 68-1 basic profile: H = P sqrt3/2, basic depth 5H/8. External groove (the space between teeth): a trapezoid P/4 wide at the root radius d/2 - 5H/8, widening by 2 tan30 per unit of radius to 7P/8 at d/2. Internal groove: P/8 wide at the major radius d/2, widening to 3P/4 at the minor radius, cut only where there is material (r >= hole radius). Pappus: volume per turn = 2 pi A rc (A the trapezoid area, rc its centroid radius from the axis); a helical sweep of L/P turns removes exactly (L/P) x that, where each end of the thread is a free end or lies inside material. A 14.6 mm boss (R=7.3, 15 tall) on a 20x20x4 plate takes a modelled M14 (P=2) over 10 mm from its free top end. The boss is thicker than the major diameter, so a die turns it down to 14 mm over the threaded length first (ring pi (7.3^2 - 7^2) 10 = 134.7743) and the groove is cut from there (5 turns, 50.18900 each). V = 1600 + pi 7.3^2 15 - 134.7743 - 5 x 50.18900 = 3725.5127 mm3. The groove's last end may nick the unturned boss by well under 0.2 mm3. Tolerance 1%: a modelled thread is a faceted helical solid (radial chord error up to 1% of the pitch on every wall, i.e. a volume deficit of about 4/3 x sag/R).
